Author: Dinesh Kumar Paliwal

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur

 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Dinesh Kumar Paliwal
 On The 14 th Of May, 2024

 Between:-
 Shivendra Kumar Verma @ Shivendra
 Vishwakarma S/O Shri Ravendra Prasad Verma,

This application coming on for admission this day, the c
 following:
 Order

This first bail application has been filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.181/2023 dated 29.04.2023 registered at Police Station- Saman,
District- Rewa (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 407,
411, 120B and 34 of IPC.

Applicant is in detention since 23.04.2024.
2.
As per the prosecution story, on 19.04.2023, Shri Chandra Hardware Private Limited, Rewa placed an order with Singhal Metallic Private Limited, Raipur for purchase of 40 ton 100 kg iron.
He also made a talk with Amit Mishra of Sonali Roadlines to transport the aforesaid consignment from Raipur to Rewa.
He was informed that Truck No.UP 70 KT 2667 belonging to Rajesh Gupta is in Raipur.
Amit Mishra gave him the mobile number of truck owner/driver Rajesh Gupta.

As per dealing, 40 ton 100 kg iron was loaded in the truck belonging to the present applicant and as transportation for Rs.6,000/- (Rupees Six Thousand) advance and Rs.22,000/- (Rupees Twenty Shivendra Kumar Verma @ Shivendra ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81031711/
1 Two Thousand) for diesel were paid.
Truck along with the consignment left from Raipur to Rewa.
In the intervening night of 20-21.04.2023, driver Rajesh Gupta informed that one tyre of truck has got burst and same is under repair.
On 21.04.2023, he informed complainant that he is in Rewa and truck has been parked near his shop as consignment had to be unloaded from truck.
It is alleged that in the morning of 22.04.2023, when complainant reached to his shop, for getting the consignment unloaded, he found truck and truck owner both missing.
His mobile phone was switched off.

F.I.R.
was registered.
In the course of investigation, stolen iron was seized and it was found that applicant had purchased stolen property having reason to believe it to be stolen property.

After investigation,
charge-sheet has been filed.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
He had placed order for purchase of the consignment and had transferred Rs.19 Lacs in the Bank account of the company.
The stock which has been seized from his shop is duly recorded in his stock book.
He had not purchased any stolen property having reason to believe the same to be stolen property.

It is further submitted that even if for the sake of argument, entire prosecution story is accepted as a gospel truth, even then applicant may be prosecuted for an offence under Section 411 of IPC which is triable by JMFC.
After investigation charge sheet has been filed.
Therefore, it is prayed that the applicant, who is first offender, may be released on bail.

4 . O n the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant and has submitted that applicant has purchased stolen property worth Rs.25,14,255/- having known it to be stolen property from the truck driver Rajesh Kumar Gupta.
5 . In this case, after investigation, charge-sheet has already been filed.
Co-accused persons have already been released on bail.

Therefore, having taken into consideration the submissions put forth by learned counsel for the applicant and other material on record including the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing anything on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the applicant is not warranted.
Consequently, this bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6 . I t is directed that applicant - Shivendra Kumar Verma @ Shivendra Vishwakarma be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7 .
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
